 Matisse Thybulle recorded 11 points (4-of-8 FGs), one rebound, one assist, three steals, one block and three three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Jazz.
 After injuries made him an afterthought in fantasy basketball in recent seasons, Thybulle may be approaching the point where he needs to be rostered in some 12-team leagues. He’s scored in double figures in two straight games, shooting a combined 6-of-13 from three in wins over the Clippers and Jazz. Thybulle still isn’t a must-add, but he may be worth a look going into the Lakers’ four-game Week 2. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Matisse Thybulle accounted for 13 points (5-of-8 FGs), one rebound, two assists, two steals, one block and three three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Clippers. 
 Could Thybulle return to relevance in fantasy basketball with the Lakers? His defense earned the veteran wing a starting spot, and he played well on both ends of the floor in Friday’s win. In addition to his three defensive contributions, Thybulle shot 3-of-6 from beyond the arc. He’s a career 34.9 percent shooter from deep, so managers shouldn’t expect high-level production there. However, the starting role makes Thybulle someone to watch, especially in deep leagues.

 Luka Dončić, Austin Reaves, Matisse Thybulle, Ziaire Williams and Walker Kessler will start Wednesday’s game against the Warriors. 
 Dončić, Reaves and Kessler starting was expected since the summer, but there were questions as to who would complete the starting five. With Thybulle and Williams starting, defense has been prioritized, and both are worth watching in deeper fantasy leagues.

 Matisse Thybulle recorded 13 points (4-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, one assist, two steals and three three-pointers in Thursday’s win over the Pelicans. 
 Injuries took Thybulle off the board for most fantasy managers even before this season began. But Thursday showed what he’s capable of when allowed to take on a more prominent role. With the Pelicans going small for significant stretches, Thybulle played 31 minutes while starting center Donovan Clingan (4/9/2/1) played 22 due to foul trouble. A disappointing end to Week 23 for Clingan was a positive one for Thybulle, who finished a blocked shot shy of a complete stat line.

 Cooper Flagg had 26 points (10-of-23 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, eight assists and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s 120-96 victory over the Thunder. 
 Flagg is averaging 25.3 points, 6.8 assists, 5.3 rebounds, 2.8 steals and 1.3 blocks through four games this year. Easily the best young player in the league, Flagg may already have elevated himself into being part of the MVP conversation.

 Stephon Castle put up 14 points (6-of-13 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, eight assists, two steals, a block, and a three in win against the Jazz. 
 Castle’s ability to put up peripheral stats will be an important part of his fantasy outlook in dynasty leagues. The main thing that is notable at this point is that he has attempted 8.2 3PT attempts per game this season which is up from 3.6 last season. In the present, if you drafted him, you’d be feeling pretty happy with the start he has had this season. He’s gotten you points, rebounds, and assists on a consistent basis. If he is shooting 3’s on a consistent basis, he could be a fantasy monster and a staple in the top 50 for years to come.

 This game had the outline of a monster fantasy performance with the rebounds and assists. Unfortunately he shot 4-17 from the field which puts a dampener on everything else.  Devin Vassell with 21 points (8-of-18 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, three steals and a three against the Jazz. 
 Vassell made some big shots in the fourth quarter to keep the Spurs in this game. While it was a good performance, he’s only up to 12.6 points, 4 rebounds, and 3.8 assists on the season. He’s a points and 3-point streamer who will occasionally have good games but is not a must in most redraft leagues. There’s too many high usage players on the team for him to be able to score like this consistently.

 While the Bulls await Nic Claxton’s return from a strained hamstring, Smith continues to provide reliable fantasy value.  Caleb Wilson accounted for 20 points (7-of-18 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, four assists, two steals, one block and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Knicks.
 Wilson has scored 20 or more points in three of his last four games and continues to improve. The Bulls’ rookie didn’t shoot as well as he can against the Knicks, but he still made an impact on both ends of the floor. The Bulls led by as much as 19 in the third quarter before the Knicks rallied to win. Wilson will be a fun player to watch develop in the years to come, and his fantasy value should only improve.

 Darryn Peterson put up 18 points (4-of-13 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, a steal, and three 3-pointers in an overtime loss to the Spurs. 
 Obviously you want Darryn to be more efficient from the field, but he got his shot attempts up which is what you want to see. He did leave the game in the first quarter with a head injury but returned. He did not close the game which is notable. He will continue to get better, and this is a good game all things considered, but the fantasy upside for this season isn’t very high.

 Buzelis is shooting just 38.8 percent from the field this season, seven percentage points lower than his career number. He was 2-of-7 inside the arc on Wednesday, but the Bulls forward made half of his six three-point attempts. Add in the full stat line, and things could have gone far worse for those rostering Buzelis.
